bluf: VaynerMedia is a US social first agency selling itself as the Modern Agency of Record, creative, media, influencer, commerce and consulting built around social for enterprise CPG, fashion, finance and restaurant brands. Its current push is AEO: a free CMO's AEO Guide and the argument that social content drives AI discovery. 19 clients are named, five observed and 14 names only; PepsiCo, Diageo, Duracell, Fanatics and Tinder sit on other tracked books. A rival should know the Horus read is Favored at percentile 90 on human provenance, while its sitemap shows 2 URLs updated in 90 days and its house sells paid social with no social pixel.

The headline claim is a roster claim (PepsiCo, Mondelez, Diageo, Bose and Coach) plus one win, H&R Block naming it social and media AOR. The record lists offices from Los Angeles and New York through Toronto, Amsterdam, London and Mexico City to Australia, India, Japan, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand; no founding year, headcount, owner or partner badge.

The sold mix leads with Creator & Influencer, scored 3: meta and headings put social at the center, an influencer and talent line and organic social cases. Two core lines score 2: AI Search / GEO (a homepage banner for a CMO's AEO guide and AEO posts by its commerce EVP) and Paid Social (the H&R Block social creative and media AOR win). Content and PR, data, programmatic and retail media score 1; paid search, SEO, web, email, CRO, B2B and local score 0: breadth 7. The one proprietary method is Comments as Creative (CasC), described on 2026-09-21 as brands treating comments on viral posts, creator videos and pop culture moments as standalone creative, pitched as the free strategy used to 10x client engagement.

Its AI posture is AEO as thought leadership: the free guide, posts arguing social content drives AI discovery, and media buyers becoming engineers; no AI visibility product or citation share shows (P1 partial), no agent line (P6 absent).

Dated moves are thin: the H&R Block AOR, dated 2025 by the press archive's 2025-09-12 lastmod, and four case studies dated 2025-10-28. No pricing signal (P5 unknown), no open job, ATS Greenhouse. Conspicuously absent: measurement or first party data depth (P4 partial), an owned audience line (P7 absent), a case study newer than 2025-10-28, and a moving sitemap: 2 URLs updated in 90 days.

openings:
The strongest judgment is the book: 14 of the 19 clients are names only, work page logos, and the five observed engagements are organic social results dated 2025-10-28, so a rival pitching PepsiCo, Diageo, Duracell, Fanatics or Tinder, each on another tracked agency's book, very likely (moderate confidence) finds no published VaynerMedia proof to argue against. Falsifier: a next compile adding dated case studies for the logo clients.

Second, the paid social contradiction: it sells paid social and holds an H&R Block media AOR, yet its site carries no social ad pixel, so a rival running its own paid social with the pixel to show likely (moderate confidence) wins that comparison. Third, AEO without a number: it sells AI discovery through a free guide and EVP posts with no audited AI visibility product, so an audited citation share leads the pitch. Fourth, P4 partial: paid media with no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth on record, and data scores 1, so a measurement led offer undercuts the media line as KJ5 raises prices. No public pricing (P5 unknown) leaves an outcome priced offer unanswered, though displacement at 29.4 says the book is unlikely to move on price.
